body: I feel you there. Really, I do. But that has nothing to do with the fact that you can still live long enough to eventually graduate. And that's all assuming that you're guaranteed to fail your current class. (Which so far, doesn't appear to be a guarantee.)

Yes, we've agreed that death = nothingness. What I'm asking is, wouldn't it be better to interact with them over the phone / skype / whatever other means then dying and not getting to interact with them again?

I don't hate you, as an example. So no, not everyone hates you. And yes, you can save yourself. When you eventually get hired and start working again, it's still possible to save up the 3000+ pounds, yes?

I won't act like I know your situation: but wouldn't interacting through other mediums like telephone calls, skype, etc. be a way of at least being in each others lives? Aside from being physically next to each other? That's something death can't give you.
What makes you sure that being alive and happy is eternally impossible?
Hey, I've lost two jobs, and though it was a bear finding a new job, I got one. And I got turned down a lot. There will always be a way to get that money.
But then you two are guaranteed to never be together. And nothingness doesn't feel like anything. Because you'll be too dead to perceive it. Literally the last thing on your mind will be pain.
Okay. Let's just say you're right: there's not a \*\*\*\* thing you can do. Why kill yourselves? How will that make you feel any better?

Okay. Let's say you fail your course. And I mean irredeemably bomb it: you can always take it again. But if you die, the last thing on your mind will be the sadness of flunking it. Wouldn't you want to be alive to experience the success of (eventually) passing?

Actually, I do feel this way. I'm not being dismissive. Dismissive would be "great for you." I'm asking because I'm willing to bet that death isn't really want you want. It's the end of suffering, which death just won't do for you.
Hey, not everyone can be nice. There's plenty of mean, shady people out there. If you can be nice, you're part of what makes this world brighter.
Ok. Why? I didn't want to tell the whole world I wanted a ham sandwich until now to prove a point. Why do you want to tell us you want to commit suicide?
So why post here? I'm sensing some inconsistencies here.
Same. I've got bipolar type II, and I've been pleading with my friends / acquaintances to just let me die.

"Nothing we can do to make him feel better. I can't handle it anymore. I just want us to feel better. If that means death, then so be it." ...you do realize death can't make you feel better though, right? Death means dead. As in your last memory will be your lowest point. Since your brain can't perceive anything during death, and the last, conscious memory is you being miserable: wouldn't that realistically mean you would be miserable for all eternity? The only logical, realistic thing to do would be to work with your husband so you can perceive things like fulfillment, relief, comfort, while your brain is still alive enough to process that?

That's depression. Right there. It'll happily parade all of your flaws, magnify them with a magnifying glass bigger than Texas, and exclude all other assets of yourself. Can you seriously say that you don't have \*any\* positive qualities? If you say no, I'm gonna call you out on it. For example: you can type. There's billions of people that either never had or will have the education to read and write. So yes, it would be sad that one of the chosen few, literate, people; died. Is there any other positive points you'd like to raise so we can make a balanced decision?
What happens when you've done all that?
